hypothesis: Arming a frozen profit floor and trail only after five consecutive causal regime-opposition decisions may protect genuine HYPE reversals without cutting regime-supported winners.
decision: Reject the exact five-decision-conditioned 25/15/10, 40/15/20, and 60/15/30 bps policies. Conditioning reduced the universal-lock damage, but every variant still lowered mean normalized HYPE return by more than 31 bps per resolved lifecycle. The tightest policy improved two HYPE outcomes, degraded three, and left three unchanged. Its apparent rescue of the latest loss is post-hoc and does not offset the earlier winner truncation. Preserve the active exit contract and grant this mechanism no execution authority.
falsifier: A prospectively frozen, profile-matched forward observer that improves after-cost mean normalized HYPE return across multiple non-adjacent opposition-triggered lifecycles without increasing loss concentration or materially truncating regime-supported winners would update this rejection.
limitations: The five-decision rule was specified after inspecting the latest HYPE loss and is not independent confirmation.
Eight resolved HYPE lifecycles remain sparse and span differing source profiles and process runs.
The exact live regime-opposition episode is not available as an independent historical development or untouched holdout sample.
Completed one-minute bars cannot reconstruct intraminute activation and trigger ordering.
Counterfactual exits reuse each actual exit fill/reference ratio and fee rate rather than submitted venue orders.
Normalized lifecycle results do not form a counterfactual shared-portfolio equity path.
The currently open aligned HYPE short is excluded from resolved comparisons.
